VERIDIAN DPDP: how it looks and how it works

A walk through every screen, role by role, with one plain sentence on what the person does there. All pictures are real screens of the product running on made-up sample data; no real person or school appears.

The idea in one line. Every week, in a few minutes, the person in charge does three things:
1. Identify
Write down what personal data you hold, where it lives and who holds it.
2. Classify
For each line, say whose data it is, whether it is about children, why you hold it and for how long.
3. Prove
Keep the records that show it: documents, breaches, requests, erasures, and a signed-off week.
The page shows a count of steps done. It is never a legal rating, and it never says "compliant".
A. Everyone: signing in B. The owner (school, university or firm owner) C. The CA or professional (partner and manager) D. Staff E. The Monday e-mail

A. Everyone: signing in

Nobody needs a password. Every person starts here.

B. The owner (school, university or firm owner)

The owner sets up the list once, then does a short routine each week: Identify, Classify, Prove.

C. The CA or professional (partner and manager)

A firm looks after many clients. The partner and the manager see them in one place; each client's owner confirms what the CA set up.

D. Staff

Staff only see the jobs that are theirs.

E. The Monday e-mail

The same weekly routine reaches people in their inbox, so they do not have to remember to open the page.

The e-mail pictures show the weekly part of the message, drawn by the same code that sends it, with made-up names. The weekly e-mail block is switched off for now; this is a preview of what it will look like.
